name: Distinguished Business Leader Scholarship (High School)
deadline: April 15 at 5:00 PM ET (year not stated; the page currently reflects the 2025-26 cycle)
apply: Use the linked Wufoo application. Upload a one-page cover letter about FBLA, business, leadership and community activities, an FBLA/educational resume, and one signed recommendation from a chapter adviser, teacher or business/community leader. The manual requires PDF uploads.
eligibility: Graduating FBLA High School members who plan to pursue postsecondary education and become actively involved in FBLA Collegiate. Must be dues-paid by March 1 and have reached the Advocate or Capstone level of the Business Achievement Awards program.
notes: The linked manual is labeled 2025-2026 and updated April 2026; the application is still labeled 2026. The next cycle is not yet confirmed. The number of $500 awards depends on contributions.

provider: Future Business Leaders of America (FBLA) and Pearson
name: FBLA x Futures Scholarship
value: $2,000 each to three recipients, paid to the college
deadline: The linked 2026 application closed April 15. The next-cycle application deadline is not published.
apply: The posted manual requires the Wufoo application, a resume outlining FBLA activities and educational achievements, and a signed chapter-adviser recommendation, uploaded as PDFs. Await the next application cycle.
eligibility: Active FBLA high school juniors or seniors, or college undergraduates, age 16 or older, who legally reside in the 50 states, District of Columbia or U.S. territories and intend to attend an accredited U.S. college or university. Selection considers leadership, academic commitment and FBLA engagement.
notes: The posted 2026 application is closed. The award supports study in 2026-2027 or 2027-2028; payment goes to the institution. The webpage requires enrollment proof by October 31, 2027 at 11:59 AM EST, while the manual contains different notification/payment timelines. Future-cycle dates need confirmation.

name: William P. Elrod Memorial Scholarship
deadline: May 1 each year
apply: Log in to the Student Member Site in the TSA Membership System to get the application materials.
eligibility: Current TSA student members.
notes: The official page does not list selection criteria; see the application in the member system.

provider: Technology Student Association (TSA) and National Technical Honor Society
name: NTHS Scholarship for TSA Members
value: Three $1,000 scholarships, awarded at the 2027 National TSA Conference
deadline: The NTHS sponsor page gives an annual September 15-May 1 application window; a dated 2027 closing deadline is not confirmed.
apply: Email the completed application with required attachments to general@tsaweb.org; get the form through the TSA Student Member Site.
eligibility: Current TSA and NTHS members. NTHS membership requires nomination by the school NTHS chapter adviser, and the school must have a current NTHS chapter.
notes: The TSA page confirms three $1,000 awards at the 2027 National TSA Conference. Application materials are in the password-protected TSA Student Member Site.

name: HOSA Scholarships
value: Multiple sponsor scholarships; the 2027 application does not publish individual award values.
deadline: April 1, 2027; no closing time or time zone is stated.
apply: Complete the linked 2027 HOSA Wufoo application. Provide GPA, optional test scores, an official or unofficial transcript, four leadership descriptions and at least two service descriptions, each at most 15 words, seven personal responses each at most 15 words, adviser details, membership/certification information and a professional headshot.
eligibility: HOSA members who are high-school seniors or postsecondary/collegiate members. The 2027 form asks for proposed major and healthcare career interests, but does not publish individual sponsor eligibility rules.
notes: The application linked from the HOSA scholarships page is now labeled 2027. Sponsor award values and additional sponsor-specific criteria are not listed in the form.

name: Key Club International Scholarships
value: The current Children’s Fund directory lists donor-specific minimums, including two Kiwanis Children’s Fund Key Club awards of at least $2,460 each, one Wagner Family award of at least $4,500, and an Indiana-only Linda Canaday award of at least $3,440. The page does not label these as 2027 award amounts.
deadline: Applications open November 1, 2026 and close February 1, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET.
apply: Create an account in Foundant and submit one universal application with a personal statement, one letter of recommendation and an unofficial transcript.
eligibility: Graduating high school members in good standing of Key Club International. Current donor awards have additional restrictions: Linda Canaday requires Indiana residence, a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale or equivalent, and two years of membership in good standing. Confirm the November 1 cycle-specific award list; Circle K awards are listed separately.
notes: The directory lists donor-specific award minimums and restrictions, but its application opportunities are posted November 1 and the page does not label the listed amounts for the 2026-27 application cycle. The Key Club calendar separately confirms November 1, 2026 to February 1, 2027. District and local Kiwanis scholarships are separate from this Children’s Fund listing.

name: PDK International Scholarships for Educators Rising Members
value: About 100 scholarships a year, from $500 to $4,000 (one-time and renewable)
deadline: PDK says 2027-28 applications will open in December 2026; its general page says application periods usually run from early January into early April, while the prior FAQ lists March 1, 2026. The 2027 closing date is not yet confirmed.
apply: Use one scholarship application through the PDK membership portal when the 2027-28 cycle opens. The current public instructions request a 250-word teaching/public-education statement, a 150-word association-involvement response, a 150-word other-activities response, up to three unofficial transcripts and one recommendation letter from someone outside your family. Confirm any changes when the new portal opens.
eligibility: Members in good standing of Educators Rising, Educators Rising Collegiate, Pi Lambda Theta or PDK Association who plan to pursue a career in public education and will be enrolled in higher education, full- or part-time, paying tuition and fees in fall of the application year. Donor-specific criteria are matched through the one application.
notes: Awards cover higher-education tuition, fees, room and board for the fall academic year. Some donor scholarships are renewable for up to four years while pursuing education; others are one-time. The FAQ does not require U.S. citizenship. PDK plans a December 2026 opening for 2027-28, but generic January-opening language conflicts and no 2027 closing date is confirmed.

name: Quill and Scroll Student Scholarships in Journalism (Nell, Gallup and Johns awards)
value: Variable scholarships determined by the Quill and Scroll Scholarship Committee for the freshman year only, paid through the institution and potentially in two installments.
deadline: The student scholarship page says applications for 2027 are open and lists May 7, 2027 as the closing date; the sentence retains an inconsistent 2026 application label.
apply: Submit the online application with two recommendations, one from a journalism teacher/adviser and one from a principal/counselor, on school letterhead as PDFs; a personal statement of at most 500 words; three examples of journalism; and a color JPG headshot no larger than 2 MB. Recommenders may email letters if school policy prevents student access.
eligibility: Current high-school seniors. Nell and Gallup awards require national winning work in a Quill and Scroll contest, including Yearbook Excellence, Writing/Photography/Multimedia or Eye on Ivy. Johns is available to all Quill and Scroll senior members. Recipients must major in journalism or a related communications area.
notes: Funds can pay tuition, room and board. Individual dollar amounts are determined by the committee and are not published. The 2027 page lists May 7, 2027, although one sentence still calls it the 2026 application.

name: SNHS Student Scholarship and Arepalli-Karumuri Family Grant
value: The published 2026 program offers $1,000 awards under two opportunities: SNHS Student Scholarship and the Arepalli-Karumuri Family Grant for a science-fair participant.
deadline: The Science National Honor Society says its 2026-27 Student Scholarship application will launch in early December 2026. It has not posted the 2027 closing date.
apply: Apply on the online scholarship platform; recommendation letters must arrive by the deadline.
eligibility: Seniors who are current members of an active SNHS chapter with a minimum cumulative GPA of 3.5. The family grant targets students who excelled in science fair competitions.
notes: The society’s new awardee page announces an early-December launch for the 2026-27 application and names the Arepalli-Karumuri grant for science-fair excellence. The $1,000 amount, 3.5 GPA floor and January 31 closing time are from the previous 2026 application and should not be used as current eligibility filters.

name: 4-H Youth in Action Awards
value: The 2027 program selected four winners, each receiving $5,000 for higher education, a year of professional/media development and national spokesperson opportunities. Nebraska 4-H also described expenses-paid trips for the winner and a chaperone.
deadline: The 2027 winners were announced September 22, 2026. The next application dates are not confirmed.
apply: Submit the Youth in Action application on 4-H.org when it opens.
eligibility: The latest application announcement required U.S. 4-H members or recent alumni ages 14-19 who demonstrate community impact. Next-cycle eligibility has not been confirmed.
notes: National 4-H Council announced the four 2027 winners in its September 22, 2026 press release. The main application pages are inaccessible; official Nebraska 4-H described the previous application deadline as April 13, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST. Next-cycle dates and criteria remain unconfirmed.

name: Eagle Scout of the Year Scholarship
value: $10,000 to the Eagle Scout of the Year; three runner-up scholarships of $2,500
deadline: Packets must reach your American Legion Department (state) by March 1, 2027. Follow any earlier local post or district deadline. Department winners advance to national headquarters by April 1, 2027.
apply: Submit the full nomination packet to the Legion department where the Scout unit is chartered, including current Scouting membership proof, official high-school transcript, school/community/religious records, Scouting leadership and Eagle project summaries, career interests, four required recommendations from religious institution, school, community and Scouting, and Scout, parent and unit-leader certifications. Department winners advance to national headquarters by April 1.
eligibility: Registered active Scouting America members who have earned the Eagle Scout Award and a religious emblem, are at least 15 and enrolled in high school, and either belong to a unit chartered to an American Legion post, auxiliary unit or SAL squadron, or have a parent or grandparent who is a current Legion, SAL or Auxiliary member.
notes: Requires a Legion-chartered unit or a parent/grandparent with current Legion-family membership; a recently deceased member may use the prior-year membership. The national winner must be available for the August convention youth delegation. Funds support accredited postsecondary study and must be used within four years after high-school graduation, excluding military duty or religious mission.

name: Gold Award Scholarship
value: The closed 2026 program offered $5,000 to one Gold Award Girl Scout per council and one from USA Girl Scouts Overseas. The 2027 award amount has not been posted.
deadline: The 2026 program ran March 13 to April 14, 2026; 2027 details not posted
apply: The previous program required four separate written responses of at most 500 words or videos of at most three minutes each, plus demographic details, headshot with photo release and confirmation of Gold Award approval. Await the 2027 instructions.
eligibility: Gold Award Girl Scouts who are high school seniors (or recent graduates) with the final report approved in GoGold within the eligibility window. Past applicants cannot reapply.
notes: The official page says the 2026 program has closed and to check back in 2027. Prior awards paid tuition, fees and required coursework books/supplies at accredited U.S. or international two/four-year or vocational/technical institutions; room and board were excluded. Funds were sent directly to the institution.

name: Frank L. Weil Memorial Eagle Scout Scholarship
value: Two one-time $5,000 scholarships
deadline: The posted 2024 application accepted postmarks from October 1 to March 31; a current-year application is not posted
apply: The linked PDF instructs applicants to email the completed application to Chairman@JewishScouting.org with one signed Scout-leader recommendation and one signed Rabbi/faith-leader recommendation. Use only the form space; extra resumes and attachments are not accepted. The form also retains postmark language, so submission timing needs clarification.
eligibility: Registered active Scouts BSA, Venturing, Exploring or Sea Scout members who are Eagle Scouts, active synagogue members and hold Ner Tamid or Etz Chaim. Must be in the final year at an accredited high school and demonstrate practical citizenship. One application per Scout. The form permits conditional consideration when rank or emblem is completed between April 1 and graduation.
notes: The form remains dated August 2024 and contains both email instructions and an October 1-March 31 postmark window. Weil offers two one-time $5,000 awards for an accredited bachelor's-degree-granting institution. Unlike Vernon and Arkans, Weil does not list financial need or FAFSA as requirements.

name: Scout of the Year
value: Recognition at local, state and national levels; the current national program page and linked rules do not publish scholarship dollar amounts.
deadline: Entry due to a local VFW Post by March 1 (annual)
apply: Submit to one local VFW Post the entry form with Scout, unit-leader and parent signatures, uniform photograph, one-page school record, up to three pages of Scouting record including the major award project, one-page community-service record and three recommendations from a Scout leader, community member and teacher/faculty member. Homeschool applicants may use a parent for the teacher recommendation.
eligibility: Registered, active Scouts who have earned the Eagle Scout Award, Girl Scout Gold Award, Venturing Summit Award or Sea Scout Quartermaster Award; maximum age 18 (still eligible if you turn 18 during the nomination year and are in high school at the deadline). Prior national Scout of the Year winners are ineligible.
notes: Current VFW overview and rules explain recognition and the local Post entry process but do not publish a current dollar amount or dated 2027 entry deadline. Older VFW winner announcements describe scholarships up to $5,000, which cannot be represented as a confirmed current prize.

name: NEHS Scholarships
value: Over $90,000 in the scholarship fund, with 30 or more recipients in an average year; individual amounts depend on submission quality and volume. At least one $5,000 Dr. William C. Johnson scholarship is awarded each year.
deadline: Fall round: September 28-October 13, 2026. Winter round: December 7, 2026-January 12, 2027. Award announcement May 3, 2027. No time zone is stated.
apply: Through AwardSpring, submit a critical analytical essay of at most 850 words including quotations/references, double-spaced in 12-point font with MLA documentation, as an anonymous PDF labeled for the prompt. Upload one accessible MOV/MP4 video of 1-2 minutes and strictly under two minutes answering both supplementary questions. Complete demographic questions and agree to provide a recipient report/photos. Students may enter either or both rounds; the higher-scoring essay is used.
eligibility: Current high-school seniors who are NEHS student members at an active chapter and plan to attend an accredited two-year college or four-year university, anywhere in the world. Any major is allowed.
notes: Fall text: Accountable by Dashka Slater. Winter text: The Nightingale by Kristin Hannah. Awards are paid directly to the institution in late summer. NEHS can hold an award for a one-year college-entry deferral; awards not accepted within one year are forfeited.

name: Joseph Adams Senior Scholarship
value: $2,000 and $1,000 scholarships
deadline: December 8, 2026 at 11:59 PM Eastern Time.
apply: The SHH sponsor submits one chapter nominee through the Google form scheduled to be posted by October 8. Upload six files: signed signatures form, original essay in Spanish or Portuguese of at most 500 words, transcript with current coursework, honors/activities list, and two signed one-page school recommendations, one from the language teacher and one from a principal, counselor or other teacher. Include a three- to five-minute uninterrupted Spanish conversation video with student and teacher visible via a viewable YouTube link.
eligibility: Graduating SHH senior members currently enrolled in Spanish or Portuguese, or who completed the school’s highest available language course and provide a counselor/administrator verification letter. Chapter sponsors and co-sponsors must be AATSP members in good standing for 2027. Only one applicant per chapter; multiple submissions disqualify all chapter candidates.
notes: Use the award in fall 2027 at a college or university. It cannot be extended beyond one academic year; delaying enrollment forfeits the award. Winners must provide college information by August 15, 2027. Follow the current instruction PDF, which restricts the second recommender more tightly than the generic scoring rubric.

provider: National Council for the Social Studies
name: Rho Kappa Scholarship
value: The latest application lists a $1,500 education grant, awarded annually in June. The 2027 award terms have not been published.
deadline: NCSS says the 2027 Rho Kappa Scholarship application will open in spring 2027. The 2027 closing date is not yet posted.
apply: The latest application requires the chapter advisor to select one student and submit a 500-word civic-engagement essay and one recommendation from a project sponsor, social studies teacher or service organization. Multiple entries disqualify the chapter.
eligibility: The latest application requires an inducted graduating senior in a Rho Kappa chapter in good standing and a 3.75 cumulative GPA or equivalent. Confirm requirements when the next application is published.
notes: NCSS now announces a spring 2027 opening, while the linked public application still reflects the closed 2026 cycle with a $1,500 grant, chapter-advisor selection, a civic-engagement essay and recommendation. Confirm 2027 amount, prompt and rules when the new form opens.

provider: Family, Career and Community Leaders of America (FCCLA)
name: FCCLA Unified Scholarship Application
value: One-time awards include the FCCLA Memorial Scholarship ($2,500 for tuition, room or board), three NTHS scholarships ($1,000 each toward tuition), Grand Hyatt hospitality ($500), Marriott hospitality ($1,000) and Zwilling culinary ($1,000 toward tuition, books, room or board).
deadline: March 1, 2027 at 11:59 PM ET
apply: Log in to the FCCLA Member Portal with your Member ID, open Surveys and Applications, and choose Scholarships to complete one unified application. The rubric linked by the current application page covers transcript, academic awards, leadership and service, college/career plans, personal responses and two recommendations.
eligibility: Active FCCLA members who are graduating high school seniors. Memorial applicants plan a four-year accredited degree; NTHS applicants must participate in both organizations. Hospitality awards require a hospitality degree at a two- or four-year institution starting fall 2027. Zwilling requires national FCCLA affiliation by May 31, 2027, a 3.0 unweighted cumulative GPA and a culinary degree starting fall 2027.
notes: The current 2027 application page explicitly directs applicants to use its linked rubric, whose header is still labeled 2025-26. Consult the member portal for the complete form.

name: CAP Cadet Academic Scholarships (CadetInvest)
value: Academic awards generally range from $1,000 to $2,500 for tuition, books, or room and board at a postsecondary school. The Board of Governors award provides $2,500 each to two cadets; other amounts vary.
deadline: Applications are projected to open December 15, 2026 at noon Central and close January 15, 2027 at noon Central, including unit and wing approval.
apply: In e-Services Registration Zone, submit the primary Scholarship application and at least one academic scholarship subevent, a resume of no more than two pages and one to three recommendations about your CAP accomplishments. Combine multiple documents of the same type; unit and wing leadership must approve before the deadline. Some awards require extra documents or an essay.
eligibility: Current active CAP cadets in good standing, with the Billy Mitchell Award or higher, who are high school seniors, graduates or GED holders and have applied to or been accepted by a postsecondary school. Enroll during the award year and maintain acceptable academic and discipline standards. No scholarship recipient from the preceding three years is eligible. Individual awards add requirements: Etheridge requires a B average; Schroder requires a STEM major and original essay; August Trust is for Arizona Wing STEM or aviation cadets; Diaz is restricted to listed Florida squadrons; Mullins is need-based for Michigan Wing cadets.
notes: This is a collection of academic awards with different eligibility rules. The Schroder essay is screened for AI-generated content.

name: AMS First-Year Undergraduate Scholarship
value: $5,000: $2,500 each for freshman and sophomore years. Second-year funding depends on successful completion of the first year.
deadline: January 31, 2027
apply: Apply online through apply.ametsoc.org with an unofficial high school transcript covering the last three years and exactly one recommendation from a teacher, counselor or professional reference. A school profile is optional; all application stages must be completed.
eligibility: U.S. citizens or permanent residents entering college full time in fall 2027, pursuing atmospheric or related oceanic or hydrologic sciences, with at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Marine biology is excluded.

name: ASA Statistics Project Competition (Grades 7 to 12)
value: First prize $300, second $200 and third $100, split equally among team members; first-place winners also receive TI graphing calculators.
deadline: June 1 each year under ASA’s published standing policy. A separate 2027 announcement and closing time are not posted; no future-year date is inferred.
apply: Submit the online entry form with an original project PDF of no more than 10 pages, including data, graphs and references. Use one-inch margins, double spacing and 12-point Times New Roman throughout, including graphs. Acknowledge adult guidance. The linked ASA entry form currently reports its submission period closed; reopening and the complete current form are unconfirmed.
eligibility: Students in grades 7 to 12 residing in the United States or Canada, individually or in teams of up to four; the highest grade determines the category. Projects must collect and analyze data to answer a statistical question. Methods beyond introductory statistics are disqualified; ethical conduct and participant privacy are required.
notes: ASA’s August 2026 results explicitly confirms the recurring June 1 deadline. The current direct-entry form is closed; verify reopening before submitting.

name: ASA Data Visualization Poster Competition (Grades K to 12)
value: First prize $300, second $200 and third $100 per grade division, split equally among collaborators. First-place winners in grades 4 to 12 also receive TI graphing calculators.
deadline: April 1 each year under ASA’s published standing policy. A separate 2027 announcement and closing time are not posted; no future-year date is inferred.
apply: If a regional competition serves your area, submit only to that regional competition. Otherwise submit the ASA online entry and a readable high-quality poster image or digital PDF. Do not submit to both routes or mail a physical poster. Include the category and title in the filename and omit identifying team or school information from the poster. No entry fee. The linked ASA entry form currently reports its submission period closed; reopening and the complete current form are unconfirmed.
eligibility: Students in grades K to 12 residing in the United States or Canada. Teams in K to 3 have no size limit; other teams may have up to four members, with the highest grade setting the category. Original posters must be 18 to 24 inches high by 24 to 30 inches wide, with at least two related graphics addressing a statistical question.
notes: ASA’s August 2026 results explicitly confirms the recurring April 1 deadline. The current direct-entry form is closed; verify reopening before submitting. Regional deadlines differ: Michigan’s published 2027 regional deadline is March 26, 2027, and top entries advance to national judging.

name: SME Education Foundation Scholarships
value: More than 60 merit and need-based programs, generally $2,500 to $20,000, with both one-time and renewable awards. Individual award renewal terms vary.
deadline: SME says the 2026-27 application is closed and the next round starts in November. Its recurring application period is November 1-February 1; the next closing year is not separately dated.
apply: Register at scholarships.smeef.org and submit one application for all eligible awards. Provide manufacturing-related short answers, transcripts, completed STEM coursework and two recommendations, including one faculty member. Pell-eligible high school seniors should submit a FAFSA Submission Summary for need-based awards.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors and current college students pursuing manufacturing-related technical degrees at accredited U.S. or Canadian colleges or universities, with a minimum 2.0 GPA. Full-time and part-time students qualify. U.S. or Canadian citizens or permanent residents and student visa holders may apply; individual awards add restrictions.
notes: This is a collection of awards with different eligibility and renewal rules.

name: ASHRAE High School Senior Scholarships
value: Four one-year scholarships of $3,000. Awards are capped at direct annual education costs; only one Society scholarship may be received per year. Former applicants and recipients may reapply if eligible.
deadline: April 1 annually; a 2027 cycle is not explicitly identified. Awards support the following fall academic year.
apply: Submit one online application, professional-goals and HVAC&R-involvement answers, a financial-need statement, an official transcript sent directly by the school, college acceptance evidence and three signed recommendations from an instructor/advisor, employer and nonfamily character reference. Arrange a local ASHRAE chapter interview and evaluation; applicants under 18 need parent authorization. AI use is prohibited.
eligibility: High school seniors entering full time into a bachelor’s-level pre-engineering, engineering or engineering technology program preparing for HVAC&R work. Require at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale OR top-30% class standing. The institution must host an active ASHRAE student branch, have ABET accreditation or an ABET memorandum, or qualifying international accreditation under the Washington or Sydney Accord. Financial need, character, leadership, service and professional potential are considered. Students already receiving full educational funding from an employer, military or other organization are excluded.
notes: Selection criteria include financial need along with character, leadership, service and potential service to the profession.

name: ASME High School Senior Scholarships
value: Latest published first-year, nonrenewable awards include 25 INSPIRE/Charles W.E. Clarke scholarships of $2,000, one INSPIRE/STEM Global Action award of $5,000, and up to five John and Elsa Gracik awards of $5,000. Funds are paid directly to the school for education expenses.
deadline: The 2026-27 application is closed; the page lists March 15 without a next-cycle year.
apply: The latest instructions use an invitation link to an online application. Provide first-semester senior grades and GPA, a teacher or mentor STEM recommendation, leadership and activity information, and family resources and expenses. Recommendations cannot be written by a parent, friend or relative.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors planning full-time study in an ABET-accredited or substantially equivalent mechanical engineering or mechanical engineering technology program by the fall after graduation. Awards differ: Clarke requires family financial need; the published SGA award specifies STEM NOLA Fellows participation in 2024-25; Gracik requires U.S. citizenship and U.S. study and considers financial need, academics, character and leadership. Confirm current donor rules when the next application opens.
notes: Listed scholarships consider financial need along with STEM involvement, character and leadership.

name: SEG Scholarships
value: $500 to $10,000 per academic year. Renewal is competitive, requires annual reapplication with two faculty recommendations and qualifying SEG participation, and is limited to six total award years.
deadline: The next application opens November 1, 2026. The page lists March 1 as the annual closing date but does not explicitly name the next closing year.
apply: Create a separate SEG scholarship account in Grantinterface and submit one application for all eligible SEG scholarships. SEG policy requires two faculty recommendation forms and transcripts; supporting documents are due by March 15 each year. Awardees must provide official transcripts if unofficial copies were used.
eligibility: High school seniors planning college the following year, and undergraduate or graduate students, with above-average grades and a curriculum leading toward applied geophysics. Students worldwide may apply; individual awards restrict citizenship, residency, specialty, university or veteran status. The policy manual also requires applications to be supported by participation in SEG activities such as membership, student-chapter or committee involvement; confirm the new form’s implementation.
notes: This is a collection of donor awards with different restrictions released annually. Awardees must provide official transcripts, a donor appreciation letter, semester transcripts and a first-semester progress report. Common annual application and supporting-document deadlines are published, but the dated 2027 closing notice and next donor list remain unconfirmed.

name: Sphinx Competition (Junior and Senior Divisions)
value: Junior Division (17 and under): $10,000, $5,000, $3,000. Senior Division (18 to 30): $50,000 Robert Frederick Smith Prize, $20,000, $10,000, $5,000 Audience Choice
deadline: October 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET
apply: Apply through the official Acceptd portal by October 20, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. ET. Semifinalists and finalists compete in Detroit January 20 to 23, 2027. Follow the portal for required audition materials.
eligibility: National competition for string musicians (violin, viola, cello or bass). Junior Division entrants are 17 or younger; Senior Division entrants are 18 to 30. The organization celebrates artistic talent and addresses barriers in Black and Latino communities.
notes: The public 2027 page confirms prizes, ages, competition dates and the application link. Review the linked application for any additional entrant or recording rules.

name: GMBS Music Scholarship Competition
value: 2026 prizes for three vocal and three instrumental winners: $10,000, $5,000 and $3,000
deadline: The 2026 deadline was April 20, 2026 at 5 PM Central according to the main page and packet instructions; one packet footer conflicts. No 2027 dates are posted.
apply: Latest rules require one category, vocal or instrumental, a signed application with parent approval, two contrasting concert-quality recordings and a statement of musical intent. The site offers an online form, while the packet directs applicants to request a Dropbox from the organizer. Ten semifinalists in each category must travel to Clarinda for live competition, a required meeting, and the winners’ stage show.
eligibility: High school seniors and college freshmen who intend to make music their future focus.
notes: The 2027 Glenn Miller Festival is scheduled June 10 to 13, 2027, but this is not a published date for the next scholarship competition. Semifinalists pay travel costs; the latest 2026 packet has conflicting deadline wording.

name: Morton Gould Young Composer Awards
value: Cash awards; current amounts could not be confirmed.
deadline: The next application dates could not be confirmed from accessible official content.
apply: Check the ASCAP Foundation program page for the current application and composition submission instructions. Current requirements could not be confirmed.
eligibility: This program recognizes young concert-music composers. Current age, residency, performing-rights affiliation and prior-award restrictions could not be confirmed.
notes: Official program and announcement pages remained inaccessible during this review.

name: Senior Brass and Voice Performance Competitions
value: National Winner $2,000, Second $1,000, Third $500, Merit Awards $100 (separately for brass and voice)
deadline: Registration opens November 1, 2026 on Acceptd; video deadline December 2, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. ET
apply: Register on Acceptd from November 1, 2026 and upload unedited, fixed-camera performance videos by December 2 at 3 PM Eastern. Show the performer’s full body and instrument, with the live pianist visible where accompaniment is required; YouTube links are not accepted. Submit all registered repertoire, which cannot change between rounds. Seven finalists per category perform live in St. Louis; the senior rehearsal, competition and winners’ concert are April 2, 3 and 4, 2027.
eligibility: Brass players (trumpet, horn, euphonium, trombone or tuba) and singers ages 15 to 18 on January 1, 2027, studying with a teacher. Entrants must reside in the U.S. during the competition year and be U.S. citizens, valid U.S. visa holders, asylees or permanent residents. Under-18 entrants need parent permission. Previous national first-place winners cannot reenter the same level and category.
notes: Nonrefundable $150 entry fee includes Acceptd. Teacher membership must be paid before registration or a $200 nonmember teacher fee applies. Entrants pay travel and lodging; optional official national pianists cost $150 for instrumentalists or $100 for singers. Winners must perform in the winners’ concert to receive money. Brass repertoire spans two periods (30-minute limit); voice uses four specified classical selections, memorized (15-minute limit).

name: Stillman Kelley National Instrumental Awards and Thelma Byrum Piano Award
value: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, $750 third, five regional awards of $500; Thelma Byrum Piano Award $750 (for further study)
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Apply at forms.nfmc-music.org with an unlisted YouTube performance link for each listed piece, scanned scores in PDF, a biography of up to 250 words and a JPG photo. Pay $10 online; membership and payment are verified. Perform 15 to 20 minutes from memory on one instrument, including an American composition; no concerti or chamber music.
eligibility: Instrumentalists who have not reached their 19th birthday by March 1. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Awards support further musical study. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter the same award; no entry in multiple NFMC divisions in one year.

name: Michael R. Edwards Graduating Senior Performance Award
value: $5,000, paid in two $2,500 installments after first- and second-semester enrollment verification.
deadline: May 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the NFMC online application and all materials together, including the performance submission, two recommendations and music-school acceptance for the immediate academic year. Perform four compositions: three contrasting periods and one American composition. Pay the $20 fee online.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors under 19 by May 1 who will pursue a music performance degree at an accredited music school and have earned at least one NFMC Federation Cup. NFMC Junior membership and U.S. citizenship are required. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter the same award.
notes: The award is for a music performance degree. Enter only one NFMC division in a year.

name: Lynn Freeman Olson Composition Awards
value: $1,500 high-school and $750 intermediate awards for further musical study; judges may withhold awards. The 2027 announcement also permits advertised amounts to be adjusted for financial shortfalls, with applicants notified.
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart). Postmark deadline; mail no more than one month before closing.
apply: Follow the award-specific mailed application rules: send the typed signed form, an original manuscript and six legible copies, postmarked by March 1 in an odd year. Do not email or upload. Submit one anonymous piano solo or piano-only ensemble composition, no more than four engraved pages and written for early-elementary to intermediate piano skill. Do not include recordings.
eligibility: Nonprofessional composers in grades 10 to 12 for the $1,500 high-school category, or grades 7 to 9 for the $750 intermediate category, who are currently studying music and are NFMC members. Works must not have been published for public use or sale. Only one original composition per entrant; arrangements are excluded. Past monetary winners cannot reenter the same category. U.S. citizenship is not required.
notes: Award-specific August 2026 rules require postal submission, despite the general NFMC online policy. Entry fee is covered by a private donor. Membership is still required.

name: Mary Alice Cox Awards (Cello or Double Bass)
value: $2,500 first, $1,500 second, $1,000 third
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the online application, 10- to 15-minute video or unlisted YouTube audition, timed repertoire list, teacher recommendation and teacher/parent performance verification together. Perform two contrasting original cello or bass works, including a published American composition. Pay $20 online.
eligibility: Cellists and double bassists who have not reached their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Awards support further musical study and may be withheld if no applicant is selected. No prior first-place winner may reenter the same award or enter multiple NFMC divisions in one year.

name: Wendell Irish Viola Awards
value: $2,000 first, $1,000 second, one $500 award in each of the 5 NFMC regions
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the online application, recorded performance, membership proof and repertoire list together at forms.nfmc-music.org and pay $10. Perform at least two pieces from contrasting style periods.
eligibility: Violists who have reached their 12th but not their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: Previous first-place winners cannot reenter. Do not enter multiple NFMC divisions in one year.

name: Martha Marcks Mack Junior Vocal Award
value: $1,500 first, $1,000 second, $500 third
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the online application, biography, headshot and high-quality unedited video or unlisted YouTube links; pay $10. Perform from memory with live piano accompaniment: Italian Baroque/Classical aria or art song; contrasting Italian/German/French aria or art song; English art song; musical-theatre song; American folk song. Announce titles and composers, following the rule’s 15- to 20-minute maximum program instruction.
eligibility: Singers in grades 10 to 12 who have not reached their 19th birthday by the application deadline. NFMC Junior Division members (individual or through a federated club) who are U.S. citizens (native-born or naturalized).
notes: The award supports further musical study. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter or enter multiple NFMC divisions in one year.

name: Marilyn Caldwell Solo Piano Awards
value: $1,250 first, $750 second
deadline: March 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the online application, memorized 10- to 15-minute piano-solo recording and repertoire list with composer nationalities together, and pay $10. Include contrasting periods and at least one American composition; no concerti.
eligibility: Pianists in grades 10 to 12 who are under 19 by March 1, NFMC Junior members and U.S. citizens. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter the same award; enter only one NFMC division per year.
notes: Only original piano-solo repertoire is normally accepted; limited faithful transcriptions are allowed when period repertoire is unavailable.

name: Lana M. Bailey Piano Concerto Awards
value: $1,500 first, $500 second
deadline: May 1, 2027 (2026-27 NFMC awards chart).
apply: Submit the online application, memorized concerto recording with orchestra or second piano, two recommendations and music-school acceptance for the following academic year together. Perform a first or last movement from a Senior Class Piano Concerto in the current Federation Festivals Bulletin. Pay $10 online.
eligibility: Graduating high school seniors under 19 by May 1 who will attend college, university or conservatory as a music major, are NFMC Junior members and U.S. citizens. Prior first-place winners cannot reenter the same award; enter only one NFMC division per year.
notes: College acceptance and two recommendations are required.

name: NSE/NPE Senior Scholarship (Traditional Scholarship)
value: One-time $1,000 for postsecondary education expenses, paid directly to the school.
deadline: May 3, 2027 (applications open October 1)
apply: Ask your teacher to select you, then use the linked Google Form and media release. Submit an uninterrupted Spanish conversation with your teacher of up to five minutes on YouTube, a persuasive Spanish essay of no more than one typed page, a seven-semester transcript or signed teacher-and-parent senior-status statement, and one recommendation from a teacher, principal or counselor. Follow the required filenames.
eligibility: Graduating seniors who scored at or above the 75th percentile on NSE/NPE in both 2024-25 and 2025-26 and take the exam in 2026-27. Only one applicant per teacher, selected from that teacher’s school. Must enter college, university or trade school the academic year immediately after graduation; no gap year. Applicants may also apply for SHH awards but may receive only one scholarship.
notes: The detailed 2027 rules make prior exam performance mandatory, although the overview only encourages medal winners to apply. Winners are notified by May 31, 2027.

name: Children of Warriors National Presidents' Scholarship
value: Fifteen $5,000 awards, three per geographic division, for undergraduate tuition, books, fees, room and board. Enrollment certification is due within 12 months of award notification; funds must be used within 24 months.
deadline: The 2027 application will be posted in early October. The published annual deadline is March 1 at 11:59 PM Eastern; the detailed rules still name March 1, 2026.
apply: The latest rules require an online essay response of at least 600 characters, veteran discharge papers or current active-duty orders, recent high school grades, written verification of 50 service hours, and two nonfamily recommendations. One recommendation must come from an educator or spiritual advisor. Service documentation must come from each organization, or a school counselor if the school arranged the service.
eligibility: The latest rules require a current high school senior or homeschool equivalent who is a direct descendant of a qualifying U.S. Armed Forces veteran or servicemember, with 50 verified community-service hours during high school. Legion family membership is not required. Already-graduated students are excluded. Confirm updated 2027 rules when published.
notes: The latest published rules require original essays and disqualify heavy AI use; judging weighs academics 40%, character/leadership 30% and the essay/application 30%.

name: Spirit of Youth Scholarship for Junior Members
value: $1,000 per department/state winner; five division winners receive $5,000 instead. State awards are paid to the school for the first semester and must be used within 24 months of high school graduation. National awards begin with $2,500; later funds require re-enrollment and a 3.0 average, with six years to use the award. Initial enrollment certification is due within 12 months of notification.
deadline: The 2027 application will be posted in early October. The published annual deadline is March 1 at 11:59 PM Eastern; the detailed rules still name March 1, 2026.
apply: The latest rules require an online essay response of at least 600 characters, recent high school grades and two nonfamily recommendations. One reference must be an educator or spiritual advisor; the other must address character, citizenship and leadership.
eligibility: The latest rules require a high school senior or equivalent who is or was an ALA Junior member, with three consecutive prior years of membership, current paid membership and at least a 3.0 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Maintain ALA membership while receiving the scholarship and attend an accredited higher-education institution. The page still identifies 2023-25 membership and 2026 current dues; confirm 2027 requirements when published.
notes: Girls State alone does not establish ALA membership. The latest rules screen essays for originality and disqualify heavy AI use.

name: Science Olympiad Founders' Scholarships
value: The Science Olympiad USA Foundation describes five $10,000 Founders’ Scholarships annually. The latest 2026 rules describe them as one-time awards paid to the college after enrollment; 2027 payment terms are not yet published.
deadline: The Foundation lists spring as the annual application period and May for award announcements. Exact class-of-2027 application dates have not been posted.
apply: The latest round requires the student to submit one final online entry personally, answering three questions with a maximum of 1,000 characters each. No one may submit on the student’s behalf; coaches may verify participation.
eligibility: Latest round: class of 2026 graduating high school seniors on a registered U.S. Division C Science Olympiad team during the 2025-26 season. Confirm class of 2027 eligibility when the next application is published.
notes: The official scholarship page has moved to /programs/scholarships.

name: NCF-Envirothon International Competition
value: Scholarships and prizes are part of the international competition. The 2027 monetary award amounts have not been announced.
deadline: Qualify through your state, province or partner nation. The international competition is July 24 to 30, 2027 in Emmitsburg, Maryland; 2027 team registration dates are not yet published.
apply: Compete through your state, provincial or partner-nation Envirothon program and obtain the representative’s certification. Qualifying teams register all participants, pay registration fees and sign competition rules and codes of conduct; adult chaperones and host-provided lodging and meals are required.
eligibility: Teams of five students from the same school, nontraditional school or youth organization, in grades 9 to 12 and ages 14 to 19 at the start of the competition. Students must complete the current-year Envirothon program or training before the qualifying competition and be affiliated with a local conservation district or equivalent agency. State/provincial programs send one team; partner nations may send up to three. Teams with fewer than five compete only as exhibitions and cannot receive awards.
notes: The 2027 current issue is Soil Health Management. NCF rules say awards will be announced before the competition; the 2027 award list, registration details and oral presentation rules have not been posted.
